Accessibility
ARIA Attributes

Spinners use role="status" and aria-label to indicate loading state to screen readers. The spinner is announced as a live region so users are informed when content is loading.

Screen Reader Support

Screen readers announce loading states. Provide descriptive aria-label text (e.g., "Loading content" or "Processing request") to give context about what is loading.

Animation Preferences

The spinner respects user preferences for reduced motion. When prefers-reduced-motion is enabled, animations are minimized or removed to accommodate users with motion sensitivity.

Focused section headers use the same grey background as the hover state (pointer or keyboard). An open section does not keep that styling unless its header still has focus—for example, after focusing another header in multi-expand mode.

Tab through the headers below or click to move focus and see the focus state.

Props
Prop	Type	Default	Description
items	AccordionItem[]	[]	Per section: title, content; optional defaultOpen and disabled
allowMultiple	boolean	false	Allow multiple items to be open
label	string	—	Optional label above the control; sets role="group" and aria-labelledby
class	string	—	Additional CSS classes on the root wrapper (.accordion-field)
Accessibility
Keyboard Navigation

Accordion headers are fully keyboard accessible. Use Tab to navigate to accordion items, and Enter or Space to toggle expansion.

ARIA Attributes

The Accordion component uses proper ARIA attributes:

Native <button> elements for section headers (keyboard and screen reader support)
aria-expanded indicates open/closed state
aria-controls associates headers with content panels
When label is set: role="group" and aria-labelledby reference the visible label
Disabled sections use the disabled attribute on the header button (removed from tab order)
Screen Reader Support

Screen readers announce the accordion header text, expansion state, and content when expanded. The relationship between headers and their content is clearly communicated.

Command Center (variant + panel)

Command Center grid, sort and filter header affordances, and zebra rows. Sample data includes PR IDs, vendors, amounts, status as color swatches, and overdue counts. The docked panel can follow a Purchase Requisitions–style pattern (summary, overdue banner, late items). Selecting a row uses the.table-row--command-center-selected class (semi-transparent tint on cells). Pass acommand-center-aside slot with CommandCenterPanel so the panel aligns with the table (toolbar stays above the table only). In React, use the commandCenterAside prop andonRowSelect on Table with variant="commandCenter". For hierarchical rows, use grouped with data-has-children and childtr elements (data-parent-id, data-depth); limit nesting to four levels.

TableCostpointGrid (Astro) props
Prop	Type	Default	Description
maxHeight	string	—	Caps the vertical scroller height (overrides the default of six visible body rows plus header).
scrollChrome	boolean	false	When true, shows horizontal scroll arrow buttons under the panes and vertical arrows on the right.
resizableSplit	boolean	true	When true, the split bar resizes the frozen vs scroll panes (pointer drag and keyboard).

Slots: frozen-thead, frozen-tbody, scroll-thead, scroll-tbody — use the same number of body rows in both panes. In the Harmony repo the source is src/components/ui/TableCostpointGrid.astro. See the examples on this page for usage.

Props
Prop	Type	Default	Description
headerVariant	'gray' | 'white' | 'none'	'gray'	Header background (ignored when variant is 'commandCenter', which uses the command-center header style via sortColumns).
variant	'default' | 'commandCenter'	'default'	Command Center: full grid borders (#E0E4EB in light), sort and filter header controls (sortColumns), body typography and cell padding aligned with default tables; default zebra striping unless striped={false}.
striped	boolean	false	Zebra rows. For variant commandCenter, defaults to true; pass striped={false} to disable.
reorderable	boolean	false	Enable row reordering via drag-and-drop. Displays a grip icon at the far left of each row.
grouped	boolean	false	Enable grouped rows with expand/collapse. Rows with data-has-children show an arrow; child rows use data-parent-id and data-depth (max 4 levels).
groupedDefaultExpanded	string	—	When grouped: comma- or space-separated data-row-id values for parents to render expanded on load (child rows must follow the parent in the body).
groupedExpandedRowIds / onGroupedExpandedRowIdsChange (React only)	string[] / fn	—	Optional controlled expansion: current expanded parent data-row-id values and callback. Use to wire Collapse/Expand all with variant commandCenter + grouped.
class	string	—	Additional CSS classes to apply to the table element
sortColumns / sortColumn / sortDirection	array / string / asc|desc	—	When sortColumns is set, Table renders a sortable header row. For commandCenter, headers also show filter icon affordances; wire behavior in your app (see React Table onFilterClick).
filter-bar (slot)	slot	—	Content for the filter bar above the table (dropdowns, chips, clear button)
command-center-toolbar (slot)	slot	—	Optional row above the table (e.g. 'As of' date or status) when using variant commandCenter
Usage Guidelines
Best Practices
Use tables only for tabular data, not for layout purposes
Keep column headers concise and descriptive
Align numerical data to the right for easy comparison
Use zebra striping for tables with many rows
Provide sorting and filtering for large data sets; use the filter bar variant with dropdowns, active filter chips, and a Clear button for narrowing by period, project, or category
Use reorderable tables when users need to customize row order; provide keyboard alternatives for accessibility where possible
Use grouped rows for hierarchical data; limit nesting to 4 levels
Accessibility

Use proper <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <th>, and <td> elements. Include scope attributes on header cells and provide a caption or aria-label for the table's purpose.
